I found 5 Chicago permits issued in 2025 with a reported cost of at least $150 million:

| Permit # | Address | Issued | Reported cost | Work |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 101068175 | 705 W Chicago Ave | 2025-08-19 | $396,200,000 | Core and shell for a new 7-story casino, parking and event center with a 34-story hotel tower |
| 101073691 | 370 N Morgan St | 2025-10-17 | $155,000,000 | Change to permit 101059401: filling in the ground-floor concrete slab and changing the lobby fireplace and its ventilation |
| 101059401 | 370 N Morgan St | 2025-07-14 | $155,000,000 | Full building permit for a new 31-story residential building |
| 101060198 | 370 N Morgan St | 2025-05-30 | $155,000,000 | Excavation for grade beams only (one phase of the same building) |
| 101050206 | 370 N Morgan St | 2025-05-23 | $155,000,000 | Caissons only (one phase of the same building) |

Four of the five permits are for one project, the 31-story building at 370 N Morgan St. Each was issued in a separate phase, and each reports the same $155 million project cost. That's how the city publishes them, so I counted all four. They are still one project, though, so don't add the costs together. Chicago's cost figures come from applicants and sometimes have typing errors, but these five look believable.

FINAL ANSWER: 101068175, 101073691, 101059401, 101060198, 101050206
